content: A third Phase III clinical trial, referred to as Study 5, assessed the efficacy of the quadrivalent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in a cohort of 4,055 males aged 16 to 26 years. This study included a subset of 598 men who self-identified as men who have sex with men (MSM). Within this subset, 299 participants received the quadrivalent HPV vaccine, while the remaining 299 were administered a placebo. A fourth Phase III clinical trial, known as Study 6, evaluated the quadrivalent HPV vaccine in 3,817 women aged 24 to 45 years. Participants in these studies received either the vaccine or an amorphous aluminum hydroxyphosphate sulfate (AAHS) control on the day of enrollment, followed by additional doses at 2 months and 6 months after the initial administration. The efficacy of the vaccine was analyzed separately for each study and collectively for all studies involving girls and women, in accordance with a pre-specified clinical protocol.
